prompt: Which statement pairs each publication with its editions and rate of change correctly?
options: CEOI: one edition and permanent; CESI: four editions and frequent change
CEOI: four editions and permanent; CESI: one edition and frequent change
CEOI: one edition and frequent change; CESI: four editions and permanent
CEOI: four editions and frequent change; CESI: one edition and permanent
explanation: Pages 11 and 12 say the CEOI is prepared in four editions for short periods and is subject to frequent change, while the CESI is prepared in only one edition and is permanent in nature.

prompt: Which statement about the relationship of CEOI items and the CESI is correct?
options: Specific items in the CESI obtain their numbers from the CEOI
Specific items in the CEOI obtain their numbers from the CESI
Items of both publications are numbered independently by the using unit
Item numbers are assigned by the signal officer of the receiving unit
explanation: Page 12 says the specific items in the CEOI obtain their numbers from the CESI.

prompt: Several commands need an identical instruction. Who prepares and distributes it?
options: Each command that uses it
The highest command involved
The signal officer of the lowest command
The commander of the using unit
explanation: Page 13 says instructions that are identical within several commands are prepared and distributed by the highest commands.

prompt: Who is responsible for each of these, in order: (1) communication at command level; (2) technical control of communications-electronics activities; (3) preparation and issuance of the CESI and CEOI?
options: Signal officer; commander; commander
Commander; commander; signal officer
Signal officer; signal officer; commander
Commander; signal officer; signal officer
explanation: Page 14 says communication is the commander's responsibility, while the signal officer prepares and issues both publications and is responsible to the commander for technical control and staff supervision.

prompt: Which identifiers distinguish (1) an individual copy and (2) a particular edition, respectively?
options: Short title; copy number
Copy number; short title
Base number; copy number
Copy number; base number
explanation: Page 15 says the copy number supports accounting of each published copy, and page 16 says the short title identifies a particular edition. The base number identifies the item (page 41).

prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes distribution from copy number?
options: Distribution specifies the units to receive copies and how many; the copy number identifies each published copy
Distribution identifies each published copy; the copy number specifies the units to receive copies
Both identify a particular edition of the publication
Distribution authenticates the order; the copy number lists the effective dates
explanation: Page 30 says the distribution item specifies the units to receive copies and the number each, and page 15 says each copy published is assigned a copy number to facilitate distribution, control and accounting.

prompt: Which statement about the CEOI editions is correct?
options: Only the 1st edition is in effect; the 1st reserve is issued to the using unit but is not in effect
The 1st reserve and 2nd reserve are both issued to the using unit but are not in effect
The 2nd reserve is issued to the using unit, while the 1st reserve is kept in the issuing headquarters
The 1st reserve is in effect together with the 1st edition until a compromise occurs
explanation: Pages 21 to 23 say the 1st edition is effective, the 2nd edition (first reserve) is issued to the using unit but not in effect, and the 3rd edition (second reserve) is not issued to the using unit and is kept in the issuing headquarters.

prompt: Which statement about the CESI is correct?
options: It normally contains classified information, so four editions are prepared
It does not normally contain classified information, so it poses no danger to communications security, and only one edition is prepared
It is kept in the storage vault of the preparing headquarters as a master copy
It is prepared for short periods and replaced when it is compromised
explanation: Page 25 says the CESI does not normally contain classified information, does not endanger communications security, and only one edition is prepared.

prompt: Which identifier lets users tell a replacement edition from the withdrawn edition?
options: Copy number
Base number
Page number
Short title
explanation: Page 16 says the short title identifies a particular edition of the CESI or CEOI, so it distinguishes a replacement edition from the one it replaces.

prompt: All registered copies of a CEOI are accounted for, but a credible report says an unauthorized person saw it. What is its status?
options: Not compromised, because every copy is accounted for
Not compromised until misuse is proven
Compromised, because exposure to unauthorized personnel counts even if no copy is missing
Compromised only if a copy number is missing
explanation: Page 17 says a CEOI/CESI known or believed to have been exposed to unauthorized personnel is compromised, and page 15 shows copy numbers only account for individual copies.

prompt: A using unit's signal officer learns that a CEOI is believed to have been exposed. Which report is sent first, and how?
options: A written report, through command channels
An immediate report, through command channels
An immediate report, by the fastest means
A written report, by the fastest means
explanation: Page 18 says the signal officer of the using unit submits an immediate or spot report by the fastest means, followed by a subsequent written report through command channels.

prompt: Which statement about the two reports on a compromise is correct?
options: The written report replaces the immediate report and omits the date and time
The written report repeats the immediate report's information and adds circumstances, persons responsible, action taken and recommendations
The immediate report must include recommendations to prevent similar occurrences
The immediate report is sent through command channels, and the written report by the fastest means
explanation: Page 18 says the written report contains the information in the immediate report plus the circumstances, person(s) responsible, action taken, recommendations and other information the commander desires.

prompt: Which part protects the communication system from fraudulent transmissions, and which part authenticates the entire publication for the commander?
options: The Index; Authentication Section
Authentication Section; Distribution entry
Authentication Section (items 20-29); the Index
Code and Cipher Section; the Index
explanation: Page 33 says the Authentication Section protects the system from fraudulent reception or transmission, and page 47 says only the index authenticates the entire CEOI/CESI for the commander.

prompt: A CEOI is confirmed compromised. Which action does the lesson prescribe?
options: Pull it out of circulation immediately and upgrade the first reserve to the first or basic edition
Keep it in service until the first reserve is reissued
Upgrade the second reserve to the basic edition and keep the compromised edition as the reserve
Withdraw the first reserve and keep using the compromised edition
explanation: Page 26 says that in case of compromise, the document is immediately pulled out of circulation and the first reserve is upgraded into the first or basic edition.

prompt: In an item number, which parts are before and after the hyphen, respectively?
options: Edition number, which indicates the edition; base number, which never changes for the item
Item number, which indicates the edition; copy number, which never changes for the item
Base number, which never changes for the item; copy number, which indicates the edition
Base number, which never changes for the item; edition number, which indicates the edition
explanation: Page 41 says the base number appears before the hyphen and is never changed for the same item, and the edition number appears after the hyphen and indicates the edition.

prompt: Which General Section items state the units to receive copies and the effective dates of items, respectively?
options: Index; Distribution
General Information; Index
Distribution; General Information
Distribution; Index
explanation: Page 30 says distribution specifies the units to receive copies, and page 29 says the index gives the effective date of each item.

prompt: Which part of the Ending lets a holder detect that pages of an item are missing?
options: The page number and total number of pages at the bottom center
The copy number below the unit designation
The item number at the bottom right
The designation of the preparing headquarters at the bottom left
explanation: Page 45 says the number of each page and the total number of pages for each item are placed at the bottom center, in line with the unit designation. The other parts identify the copy, item and preparing headquarters.

prompt: Which topics does General Information cover, as detailed as possible?
options: Type of radio, station per net, call signs and frequencies
Telephone directory, communication designators and wire tagging code
Security, communication media, message preparation and other information the commander desires
Panel codes, recognition signals and pyrotechnic signals
explanation: Page 31 says general information covers security, communication media, message preparation and other information the commander desires. The other options describe the Radio, Wire and Visual and Sonic Sections (pages 35 to 37).

prompt: Besides titles, numbers and dates, the Index of the CESI and CEOI contains which two portions?
options: Short title and copy number
General information and messenger schedules
Authentication and distribution portions
Base number and edition number
explanation: Pages 29, 30 and 47 say the index lists titles, numbers and effective dates, and also contains the authentication and distribution portions.

prompt: Where are these heading elements located: designation of the preparing headquarters, title with short title, and item number?
options: Upper left; upper right; center in line with the unit designation
Upper right; upper left; center in line with the unit designation
Upper left; upper right; bottom right
Upper left; center; upper right
explanation: Pages 39 to 41 place the preparing headquarters designation at the upper left, the specific title and short title at the upper right, and the item number at the center in line with the unit designation.
